subject.title: fix(cron): bound cron quarantine sidecar file reads

question: Should OpenClaw accept an 8 MiB fail-fast cap for existing cron quarantine sidecars as the permanent safety boundary?
rationale: The code fix is straightforward, but the new cap changes how already-persisted oversized quarantine sidecars behave during doctor or cron recovery.

options.title: Accept 8 MiB after proof
options.body: Treat larger quarantine sidecars as corrupt or hostile data, require redacted real behavior proof, and allow the small hardening to land.

options.title: Request a different recovery path
options.body: Ask the contributor to add operator-facing cleanup guidance or choose a different cap before merge.

options.title: Reject the cap
options.body: Keep current read behavior and pursue a broader cron quarantine storage design instead.

recommendation.title: Accept 8 MiB after proof
recommendation.body: Treat larger quarantine sidecars as corrupt or hostile data, require redacted real behavior proof, and allow the small hardening to land.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent cron SQLite/store refactors and database-first policy work make this the clearest routing candidate for the compatibility decision.
